title: Real Madrid Player Ratings vs. Valencia: Los Blancos Cruise, Apply Pressure to Leaders
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasNov 7, 2026Real Madrid have a perfect record since the September–October international break.  / Clive Brunskill/Getty ImagesReal Madrid kept the good times rolling with a comfortable 3–0 win away against Valencia on Saturday night to extend their winning streak and continue their assault on the summit of La Liga.
It was a tricky start of the game for Real Madrid, who struggled to bypass a stout Valencia low-block as Javier Aguirre’s side seemed only interested in destroying Madrid’s attacks.

But Los Blancos wouldn’t be denied and took the lead 26 minutes in with the latest long distance rocket from captain Federico Valverde. The goal eased the tension, and after three minutes of uncontested possession, Los Blancos doubled their advantage in the 36th minute when Arda Güler volleyed home a deflected Jude Bellingham cross.

Real Madrid dominated the second half against the out-of-sorts hosts, and after multiple opportunities to increase the lead, Kylian Mbappé finally added a third when he went around the goalkeeper to bag his 13th league goal of the term. To make matters worse for Valencia, captain José Gayà got sent off in the twilight of the match.

Los Blancos have now won eight straight in all competitions entering the November international break. Mourinho’s men handled their business and will spend the night level with Barcelona atop the La Liga standings with the Catalans visiting Atlético Madrid on Sunday in a marquee clash in the title race.

Fede Valverde gave Los Blancos the lead with a thumping hit.  / M Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesScoring the opener was always going to be the most important, yet most difficult mission of Madrid’s trip to Mestalla.

José Mourinho teased this was “one of the most difficult games of the season,” prior to the match. With Los Blancos facing a team and a manager that “aren’t concerned about playing marvelously well,” rescuing a result is all that matters.

Mourinho’s words were prophetic as Real Madrid were forced to get in a mud fight from the start. Valencia seemed content with the game ending scoreless from the moment the starting whistle sounded, defending deep with all their might and frustating Los Blancos with constant fouls that interrupted play and never allowed the visitors to get in a rhythm.

One of those fouls led to a dangerous free kick that Kylian Mbappé shot straight at the wall, but the rebound couldn’t have been kinder. The ball fell straight into Valverde’s path on the edge of the box, and after a perfect first touch, Madrid’s captain fired a low driven bullet into the bottom corner to give Los Blancos the lead just before the half hour mark.

At last, Valverde gave Los Blancos daylight and the advantage they so desperately needed to destroy Valencia’s game plan and control the game. Güler bagged the second less than 10 minutes later, and the game was effectively over by the time the halftime whistle blew.
Arda Güler’s stellar season continued.     / M Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty Images*Ratings Provided by FotMob*
GK: Thibaut Courtois—7.9: He was never going to be tested constantly, but the two shots on target he faced were brilliantly dealt with.
RB: Federico Valverde—8.2: An argument could be made that there is no better ball striker from the edge of the box than Valverde. Brilliant goal and defensively stout.

CB: Ibrahima Konaté—7.5: Arnaut Danjuma caused him some issues early, but Konaté eventually grew into the game and was beyond solid. A perfectly timed sliding tackle on Umar Sadiq, who would’ve been through on goal was the highlight of a fine showing from the Frenchman.
CB: Dean Huijsen—7.8: Dominant showing from Huijsen, who was a wall defensively and regularly helped Madrid progress up the pitch with accurate line-breaking passes.

LB: Marc Cucurella—8.1: Embraced Valencia’s gritty, at times dirty style and fought fire with fire. Protected the left flank, contributed to recovering possession constantly and was nearly flawless in his distribution.

DM: Bernardo Silva—7.6: Amid the chaos that was the opening exchanges, the game slowed down when the ball found it’s way to Silva. He offered clarity and creativity, finishing the game with the most chances created of any player on the pitch (four).
DM: Aurélien Tchouaméni—7.4: Lacked urgency in possession at times and a costly turnover nearly was converted into Valencia’s opener.
RW: Arda Güler—8.9: Another goal and assist for Güler, who has arguably been Real Madrid’s best player this season.
